sections.instruction: State fully the grounds upon which the waiver is being requested. Include any mitigating circumstances. Attach supporting documents as separate PDFs. The SEA will rely entirely on what is provided here.
sections.default:
I am applying on grounds of significant life and work experience and a justifiable reason for academic divergence: my Matriculation, completed in South Africa when I relocated mid–A-level studies, is not recognised under UK equivalency rules — an administrative incompatibility, not a failure of performance, as my GCSE results demonstrate.

During the years my peers were at university I cycled solo from Geneva to Jerusalem (navigating a Foreign Office hostage advisory in Syria en route) and across the United States, traversed the Jostedalsbreen Glacier, climbed Kilimanjaro, all major peaks on Mount Kenya and the Rwenzori Mountains — the latter requiring me to negotiate a 41-man UPDF armed platoon from senior Ugandan military commanders including the operational commander Brigadier General James Kazini, in order to enter a national park closed for four years due to active ADF insurgency — and briefed President Museveni on an outcome that directly led to the park's reopening.

In 2006 I identified a fatal flaw in the official Tanzanian government investigation into three tourist deaths on Kilimanjaro's Western Breach, convinced the Director General of TANAPA to allow me to lead a field investigation with senior rangers, and produced the finding that redesigned the route still in use today. I have since founded and operated three international expedition companies across Tanzania, Morocco and Nepal, led or overseen expeditions for more than 13,000 climbers at altitude up to 5,895m, built a suite of commercial software platforms as sole developer, achieved Distinctions in all four modules of an Open University LLB to date, passed all seven PPL theoretical examinations (training now resumed after COVID interruption), and set two Kilimanjaro endurance records in July 2026. I am 48, a father of five including two infants, and was personally encouraged to seek a commission with the Royal Welch Fusiliers as a teenager by my second cousin, who subsequently commanded the Royal Welsh Regiment. The attached letter sets out the full account with supporting evidence and footnotes.
